subject: science
passage: Geckos can run up glass windows and even hang upside down from ceilings, yet their feet are not sticky. Instead, each toe is covered with ridges that hold millions of tiny hairs called setae. The tip of each hair splits into hundreds of even smaller branches. Because these branches touch a surface so closely, weak attractive forces between molecules hold the gecko in place. Added together, these forces easily support the animal's weight.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To explain how the structure of a gecko's feet lets it cling to smooth surfaces
choices.B: To argue that geckos are better climbers than any other animal
choices.C: To point out that the tips of gecko hairs split into smaller branches
choices.D: To describe the different places where geckos usually live

explanation.why: The text opens with a puzzle: geckos cling to glass and ceilings even though "their feet are not sticky." Every later sentence explains part of the answer, from the ridges and hairs to the "weak attractive forces between molecules." So the text's purpose is to explain how the feet work.
explanation.A: Correct. The whole text explains how the toes' ridges, hairs, and tiny branches let a gecko hold onto surfaces like glass.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text never compares geckos with other animals, so it does not argue that they are the best climbers.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The splitting hair tips are one step in the explanation, not the purpose of the whole text.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Windows and ceilings are mentioned only as surfaces geckos can climb; the text does not discuss where geckos live.
